rulings.resolution: the Widow's Walk FAQ errata adds the token step; the 1st-edition FAQ rules that each character gets each of these rooms' boosts once per game, and the Widow's Walk rules list this room among those that take an explorer token. The rulebook says the stairs reach the Foyer through a secret door, but not which frame that is, nor whether the other frame can join a second basement room.
rulings.resolution: the frame at the head of the stairs, beside "Leads to and from Foyer", is the secret door to the Foyer and takes no tile; the tile joins the basement only at the foot of the stairs. rulings.resolution: errata. The Plant leads to the Tree House's larger door, which connects to the upper-floor or roof room; the FAQ changes the tile's second sentence to "This room's larger door is adjacent to that door." Source: https://www.dropbox.com/s/3y34f1s2tn6o4mx/Widow%27s%20Walk%20FAQ%20KB%2012.6.161.pdf?dl=0

vault.title: Vault
lines: You may try a Knowledge roll of 6+ to open the vault and empty it.

rulings.note: the tile doesn't say what "empty it" gives you, or how many cards. The tile shows an event symbol and two item symbols, and the rulebook's symbol rule would have the discoverer draw all three.
rulings.resolution: the two item symbols are the vault's contents. Discovering the Vault draws only its event card; the explorer who opens it draws 2 item cards, and the Vault Empty token goes on the tile. The 1st-edition FAQ says that on the turn you discover the Vault you draw an event card and may then try to open it, and BGG players describe opening it as drawing two item cards. The 1st-edition tile text is the same ("open and empty the vault"). Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://daviau1.rssing.com/chan-5960803/article58898.html (BGG thread "Purpose of Vault Empty token?")

rulings.note: the Vault is a barrier room (rules.md, p. 7), but with one door its far side is only the inside of the vault, and the rules don't say whether opening it takes you in there.
rulings.resolution: every explorer in the Vault is outside its door (rules.md, p. 8), and opening it empties it without anyone going in, so no explorer is ever on its far side and the game tracks no side in the Vault. With one door there is nothing beyond the far side to move on to, and the contents are the only reason to go in. Research: none beyond the rulebook.

widows-walk.title: Widow's Walk
lines: Knowledge rolls made here get +1 to the result. Speed rolls made here get -1 to the result, but the result can't go below 0.

a-moment-of-hope.title: A Moment of Hope
lines: Put the Blessing token in this room.
While a hero is in this room, that hero rolls 1 extra die on every trait roll, to a "maximum of 8 dice".

rulings.note: the card says "trait rolls" without saying whether an attack, which is rolled on a trait, counts as one; and it names only heroes, so whether a traitor in the room gets the extra die rests on that one word.
rulings.resolution: attacks are not trait rolls, so the Blessing never adds a die to combat; and the bonus is for heroes only, not the traitor (the 1st-edition card said "each explorer" and the FAQ corrected it to "each hero", which the 2nd-edition card now prints). Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: there are no heroes before the haunt starts (rules p. 3: explorers become heroes or the traitor when the haunt is revealed), so read literally the Blessing does nothing until then.
rulings.resolution: before the haunt every explorer counts as a hero for this card, and from the haunt on only the heroes do. The 1st-edition card gave the die to "each explorer", and the FAQ changed it to "each hero" only to keep it from the traitor; nothing suggests the designers meant a card drawn in the exploration phase to sit idle until the haunt. Research: no ruling found on BGG or in the FAQ. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

acupuncture.title: Acupuncture
lines: You may go to an adjacent room that has already been discovered and lose 1 Sanity. If you don't, you must attempt a Might roll.
Roll: Result
0–2: Lose 1 Speed and 1 Might.
3–4: Gain 1 Speed and 1 Might.
5+: Gain 1 Speed, 1 Might and 1 Sanity.

rulings.note: the card is printed "Go to an adjacent, discovered room and lose 1 Sanity, or attempt a Might roll", which can be read as going to the adjacent room either way. The text above carries the official correction.
rulings.resolution: you go to the adjacent room only if you take the Sanity loss; otherwise you stay and attempt the Might roll. The Widow's Walk FAQ rewrites the card as "You may go to an adjacent, discovered room and lose 1 Sanity. If you don't, attempt a Might roll". Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

adrenaline-shot.title: Adrenaline Shot

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether an attack or defense roll counts as a "trait roll".

amulet-of-the-ages.title: Amulet of the Ages

angel-feather.title: Angel Feather
lines: When you attempt a roll of any kind, you may name a number from 0 to 8 and use it as the result instead of rolling the dice.
Discard this item after you use it.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether it can be used outside your own turn, such as on a defense roll.
rulings.resolution: It can. The Angel Feather, the Lucky Stone and the Skull omen are the only cards a player may use outside their own turn. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the number named can be higher than the roll's dice could make, and higher than the top row of the table the roll is read on (5 on the Mystic Elevator's 2 dice, whose table stops at 4). Nothing says what such a result does.
rulings.resolution: a result above a table's top row takes the top row, as any bonus that pushes a roll past its table does. The card's 0 to 8 is kept as printed, since naming a high number is the card's whole point and the table's top row is what a player who names one is reaching for. Research: no ruling found on BGG or in the FAQ.

angry-being.title: Angry Being

Roll: Result

2–4: Take 1 die of mental damage.
0–1: Take 1 die of mental damage and 1 die of physical damage.

armor.title: Armor
lines: Every time you take physical damage ("not just once per turn"), reduce that damage by 1 point.
This item can't be stolen.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether it also reduces an effect that tells you to "lose" Might or Speed, rather than to take physical damage, or whether it stops an attacker from stealing your other items.
rulings.resolution: It does neither. The Armor reduces only physical damage, such as combat damage. It doesn't apply when a card or room tells you to lose Might or Speed, and it doesn't stop an attacker who beats you by 2 or more from stealing another item instead. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: The card says only that the Armor can't be stolen. The rulebook says an item that can't be traded can't be stolen, but not the reverse, so it is unclear whether the Armor can be traded.
rulings.resolution: The card is correct and the card wins over the rulebook: the Armor can't be stolen but can be traded, dropped and picked up. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

axe.title: Axe
lines: When you make a Might attack with this weapon, roll 1 extra die (maximum of 8 dice).
You can't use another weapon while using this one.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether the extra die also applies when you defend.
rulings.resolution: It doesn't; the bonus is only for attacking. Using a weapon is optional, and an explorer carrying several weapons chooses which one to use in each attack. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

bell.title: Bell
lines: When you get it, gain 1 Sanity.
If you lose the Bell, lose 1 Sanity.
Once during your turn, after the haunt is revealed, you may attempt a Sanity roll to use the Bell (results below).
Roll: Result
5+: Move any number of unimpeded heroes 1 space closer to you.
0–4: The traitor may move any number of monsters 1 space closer to you. (If you are the traitor, this result has no effect.) If there is no traitor, all monsters move 1 space closer to you.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say what "1 space closer" means, which heroes are "unimpeded", or whether these moves cost movement, meet the slowing from opponents, or count as the moved figure's own move.
rulings.resolution: a figure moved 1 space closer goes through a connecting door into an adjacent room that is one room nearer to you along a route. Distance is measured as for "nearest" elsewhere, in rooms entered (cards/events.md). A figure already in your room, or with no route to you, can't move. The Bell's user chooses which heroes move on a 5+, and the traitor chooses which monsters move on a 0–4, any number of them, zero included, and the route when several tie. "Unimpeded" heroes are those who could move on their own, not trapped by Webs, Debris or a monster's grip (1st-edition FAQ). The move is a pull, not the figure's own movement: it spends no one's movement, ignores the slowing from opponents, and gives the moved figure no other action. A monster pulled this way doesn't attack, and a haunt rule tied to spending movement (such as haunt 13's escapes) doesn't fire. The Spirit Board's monster pull works the same way. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

bite.title: Bite
lines: When you draw this card, the player on your right makes a Might 4 attack against you on behalf of the unseen "something" (which then flees).

blood-dagger.title: Blood Dagger
lines: When you make a Might attack with this weapon, roll 3 extra dice (maximum of 8 dice). If you do, lose 1 Speed.
You can't use another weapon while using this one.

rulings.note: The rulebook says only a tradable item can be stolen, yet this untradable card says what happens when it is stolen. The card also doesn't say whether you may carry it without using it.
rulings.resolution: It can be stolen, and you take the 2 dice of physical damage when it is, whether or not you ever used it. Using it is optional: if you don't add its 3 dice to an attack, you don't lose the Speed. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1701137

bloodstone.title: Bloodstone
lines: Once per turn, you may lose 1 from any trait to add 2 dice to your trait roll (maximum of 8 dice).
