bloody-vision.title: Bloody Vision
lines: You must attempt a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 Sanity.
2–3: Lose 1 Sanity.
0–1: If an explorer or monster is in your room or an adjacent room, you must attack it "(if you can)". If possible, pick the explorer with the lowest Might.

rulings.note: the 0–1 result does not say what happens when several monsters (and no explorer) qualify, or whether a monster can be chosen over an explorer; it only says to prefer the lowest-Might explorer "if possible".
rulings.resolution: an explorer comes first. If any explorer is in your room or an adjacent one, you must attack the one with the lowest Might, choosing among ties; only when no explorer is in reach do you attack a monster, of your choice. "If possible, pick the explorer" reads as a preference for explorers, and the card's horror is turning on a companion. One BGG reply reads it as a free choice between explorers and monsters (https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2133898); it is a single post, not a consensus. Earlier research: no ruling found on choosing among monsters or between a monster and an explorer. The designer did confirm that the card overrides the normal rules, giving a one-time attack into an adjacent room. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/74215

rulings.note: the card doesn't say how its attack works on an explorer in an adjacent room rather than your own, or whether you may use a weapon in it.
rulings.resolution: it is an ordinary attack that you make, so you may use a weapon or the Ring as in any attack, but an attack on an explorer in another room follows the distance-attack rules (rules p. 13): if they beat you, you take no damage, and you can't steal from them. The rulebook calls an attack on someone in another room a distance attack, and the designer's ruling that the card gives "a one-time attack into an adjacent room" adds reach, not a new kind of attack. Research: no ruling found.

rulings.note: after the haunt, the card doesn't say whether its attack counts as your one attack of the turn, or whether it still happens if you have already attacked.
rulings.resolution: it is the card's attack, outside your attack action. It doesn't use up your attack of the turn, and having attacked already doesn't stop it. "(if you can)" means a target you are able to attack: in reach, on your side of any barrier, and not one your attack's trait can't reach. The designer called the card's attack a one-time exception to the normal rules, which it already is before the haunt, when no one may attack at all. Heroes are explorers, so after the haunt the lowest-Might explorer in reach may be a fellow hero or a sleeping traitor, and the card makes you attack them. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/74215

blueprint.title: Blueprint
lines: When you roll for your movement, or roll to enter, exit or cross a room, you may choose the result instead.
You may travel between rooms that have a dumbwaiter (the card prints the word followed by the dumbwaiter icon).

rulings.note: The card doesn't say what the move between dumbwaiter rooms costs. The Widow's Walk rule sheet's dumbwaiter rule moves you only to a landing, for 1 extra space of movement.
rulings.resolution: No official, designer or community ruling found. The only BGG answer touching it says traitors use dumbwaiters like other explorers, which doesn't settle the Blueprint's cost. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2534498

book.title: Book
lines: Gain 2 Knowledge now.
If you lose the Book, lose 2 Knowledge.
Make a haunt roll now.

boomstick.title: Boomstick
lines: When you draw this card, place 2 item tokens on it.
Discard a token to make a Speed 7 attack instead of a Might attack.
When no tokens are left, discard this item.
You can't use another weapon while using this one.

rulings.note: "Speed 7 attack" is not defined on the card. Other cards' "Might 4 attack" means rolling 4 dice, so it probably means you roll 7 dice in place of your Speed, but the card doesn't say so. Unlike the Revolver, it also doesn't say what the defender rolls or what kind of damage the attack deals.
rulings.resolution: No official, designer or community ruling found; the BGG Rules forum has no thread on the Boomstick.

bottle.title: Bottle
lines: Once during your turn, after the haunt is revealed, you may roll 3 dice and drink from the Bottle (results below).
Discard this item after you use it.
Roll: Result
6: Choose a room and put your explorer there.
5: Gain 2 Might and 2 Speed.
4: Gain 2 Knowledge and 2 Sanity.
3: Gain 1 Knowledge and lose 1 Might.
2: Lose 2 Knowledge and 2 Sanity.
1: Lose 2 Might and 2 Speed.
0: Lose 2 from each trait.

box.title: Box
lines: When you draw this card, draw an item card and place it on the Box.
The item in the Box can't be dropped or traded.
If someone would steal the item in the Box, you may discard the Box instead.
On your turn, you may take the item out of the Box and put a different item you possess into it.
If the Box is empty, you may put an item into it.
The Box can't be stolen.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: The card does not say what happens to an item taken out of the Box, or whether the item in the Box can still be used while it is there.
rulings.resolution: an item taken out of the Box goes back to your ordinary possessions, and an item in the Box still counts as yours (an item that changed your traits is not "lost" by going in). A player reported a publisher answer that an item in the Box can't be used, and that swapping gives you use of the new item at the cost of the old; another player disputed it as not on the card, so whether a boxed item can be used stays open. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2534498, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2425410, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1658494

rulings.note: The card does not say whether the swap or the "put an item in an empty Box" action is limited to once per turn.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found for the Box. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2425410, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1658494

burial-mound.title: Burial Mound
lines: Put the Burial Mound token in this room.
After the haunt has been revealed, whenever an explorer leaves this room, the corpse attacks that explorer: the player on that explorer's right makes a Might 4 attack against them.
If the explorer wins that fight by 3 or more, discard the Burial Mound token.

burning-man.title: Burning Man
lines: You must attempt a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 Sanity.
2–3: Put your explorer in the Entrance Hall.
0–1: Take 1 die of physical damage, then take 1 die of mental damage.

camcorder.title: Camcorder
lines: When you draw this card, place triangular Knowledge Roll tokens on it, one for each explorer.
An explorer who has the Camcorder may take a Knowledge Roll token to gain 1 Knowledge.
You may not take a Knowledge Roll token if you already have one.
When no tokens are left on the card, discard this card and all of those Knowledge Roll tokens.

rulings.note: The card writes the token name as both "Knowledge Roll token" and "Knowledge roll tokens". It doesn't say whether taking a token is limited to once per turn. "All those Knowledge roll tokens" seems to mean the tokens explorers have already taken, and the card doesn't say whether discarding them takes back the Knowledge they gave.
rulings.resolution: One BGG answer says discarding the tokens doesn't take the Knowledge back and that each explorer can take at most one token, but no other answer confirms it and there is no official or designer ruling. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2529368

candle.title: Candle
lines: When you draw an event card, roll 1 extra die (maximum of 8 dice) for that event's trait rolls.
If you have the Bell, the Book and the Candle, gain 2 in each trait.
The first time you lose any one of those 3 items later in the game, lose 2 from each trait.

rulings.note: The Book isn't in the items deck. It's presumably the Book omen.
rulings.resolution: The 1st-edition FAQ calls the Book an omen that is also an item, so the Book omen is the third of the set. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether an event that makes you fight counts as one of "that event's trait rolls".
rulings.resolution: It doesn't. Combat is not a trait roll, so the Candle adds no die to an attack or defense roll. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether the set bonus comes back if you complete the set again after losing it.
rulings.resolution: it comes back each time you hold all three again, and only the first loss after that takes it back, because the card's bonus and loss are tied to holding the set, and a set rebuilt is a set held.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say which rolls count as "that event's trait rolls": only those made while the event is read, or also later ones, and whether another explorer's roll for your event counts.
rulings.resolution: the extra die goes to every trait roll you make for an event you drew, for as long as that event is in play, and never to another explorer's roll, because the card ties the die to your drawing the event and to your rolls.

cat.title: Cat
lines: Before one of your trait rolls, you may call on the Cat for luck: roll 1 die and apply the result below to that trait roll.
This omen can't be dropped, traded, or stolen.
Make a haunt roll now.
Roll: Result
0: Subtract 2 from the result of that trait roll.
1+: Add 2 to the result of that trait roll.

rulings.note: No per-turn limit is printed for the Cat.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found. A single forum answer says the Cat can also help attack rolls, which is a separate question. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2492582

ceremonial-robe.title: Ceremonial Robe
lines: Once per turn, when you make a Sanity or Knowledge roll, you may reroll any number of the dice from that roll.

chainsaw.title: Chainsaw
lines: If you make chainsaw noises, add 1 die to your Might roll. This also works when you defend.
You can't use another weapon while using this one.

rulings.note: The card gives no maximum-dice cap, unlike the other weapons.
rulings.resolution: No ruling found. The rulebook states no general dice cap beyond the game having 8 dice.

chalk.title: Chalk
lines: On defense rolls, you may roll Knowledge instead of Might.

closet-door.title: Closet Door
lines: Put the Closet token in this room.
Once during each explorer's turn, that explorer may roll 2 dice to open the Closet.
Roll: Result
4: Draw an item card.
2–3: Draw an event card.
0–1: Draw an event card and remove the Closet token.

rulings.note: the card does not say the explorer must be in the Closet's room to roll; presumably they must be.
rulings.resolution: you must be in the Closet's room to roll. The token marks a place in the house, and a roll from anywhere would make it pointless. Research: no ruling found. BGG threads on the Closet ask other questions (whether drawing from it ends your movement) and leave even that unsettled. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/930903

contract.title: Contract
lines: You may choose to sign the contract. If you sign, attempt a Knowledge roll. If you don't sign, nothing happens.
Roll: Result
0–1: Lose 1 Sanity.
2–3: Lose 1 Sanity. Draw an item card.
4: Draw an item card.
5+: Gain 1 Sanity. Draw an item card.

rulings.note: the results mention keeping or losing "your soul", but that is flavour only; no game effect is attached to it.
rulings.resolution: no outside ruling is needed for the card itself, which attaches no effect to the soul. Not researched further; recheck when the Widow's Walk haunts are recorded, in case one refers to it.

creepy-crawlies.title: Creepy Crawlies
lines: You must attempt a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
5+: Gain 1 Sanity.
1–4: Lose 1 Sanity.
0: Lose 2 Sanity.

creepy-puppet.title: Creepy Puppet
lines: The player on your right makes a Might 4 attack against you on behalf of the Creepy Puppet. You defend normally, rolling dice equal to your Might.
If this attack deals you any damage, the explorer who has the Spear gains 2 Might, unless you are the one with the Spear.

rulings.note: if nobody has the Spear, the Might gain has no recipient; the card does not address this.
rulings.resolution: nobody gains the 2 Might; the attack and its damage still happen. The gain belongs to the Spear's holder, so with no holder it lapses. Research: no ruling found on the no-Spear case. The one BGG thread on the card only confirms points the card already prints: it resolves once, when drawn, and the drawer gains nothing if they hold the Spear. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/547560

crystal-ball.title: Crystal Ball
lines: Once during your turn, after the haunt is revealed, you may attempt a Knowledge roll to look into the Crystal Ball, with the results below.
Make a haunt roll now.
Roll: Result
4+: Search the item or event stack for a card of your choice, shuffle that stack, then put the chosen card on top of it.
1–3: Lose 1 Sanity.
0: Lose 2 Sanity.

rulings.note: The card does not say whether the search includes the discard pile.
rulings.resolution: only the undrawn item or event stack is searched, not discarded cards. The 1st-edition FAQ also ruled the Crystal Ball can't search the room stack, which the 2nd-edition card already reflects. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

dark-dice.title: Dark Dice
lines: Once per turn, you may roll 3 dice (results below).
Roll: Result
6: Move to the location of any explorer not revealed as a traitor.
5: Move one other explorer in the same room into an adjacent room.
4: Gain 1 in a physical trait.
3: Immediately move into an adjacent room (no movement cost).
2: Gain 1 in a mental trait.
1: Draw an event card.
0: Reduce all of your traits to the lowest value above the skull symbol. Discard the Dark Dice.

debris.title: Debris
lines: You must attempt a Speed roll.
If you end up buried (a 0–2 result), keep this card. While buried you can't do anything until freed.
Once during each explorer's turn, that explorer may attempt a Might roll to free you; you may also attempt this roll yourself. A result of 4+ frees you.
After 3 failed attempts to free you, you break free automatically on your next turn and take that turn normally.
Discard this card once you are free.
Roll: Result
3+: Gain 1 Speed.
1–2: You are buried. Take 1 die of physical damage.
0: You are buried. Take 2 dice of physical damage.

rulings.note: the card does not say whether a helping explorer must be in your room to attempt the Might roll.
rulings.resolution: a helper must be in your room. BGG threads 598908, 923197 and 1107717 read it so against one dissenter, who concedes "logically the player needs to be in the same room", and the 1st-edition haunt 17 web rule, worded like this card, says "in the same room" (https://www.orderofgamers.com/downloads/BetrayalHouseHill_v4.2.pdf). The Speed roll you make on drawing the card is not an attempt to free you: those are the Might rolls, so 3 of them must fail before you break free. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/598908, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/923197, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1107717

device.title: Device
lines: At the end of your turn, if you are in the same room as an opponent, gain 1 Knowledge.
You may discard this card to add 3 dice to your attack roll. You may only use that attack to steal something.

disquieting-sounds.title: Disquieting Sounds
lines: Roll 6 dice. If the total is equal to or greater than the number of omens revealed so far, gain 1 Sanity. Otherwise, take 1 die of mental damage.

dog.title: Dog
lines: Gain 1 Might and 1 Sanity now.
If you lose custody of the Dog, lose 1 Might and 1 Sanity.
Represent the Dog with a small monster token placed in your room (use a token whose color differs from any other monsters).
Once during your turn, the Dog may move to any explored room up to 6 spaces away, using doors and stairs, then return. Before returning it may pick up, carry, and/or drop 1 item.
Opponents don't slow the Dog.
The Dog can't use one-way passages or rooms that require a roll.
The Dog can't carry items that slow movement.
This omen can't be dropped, traded, or stolen.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: The card borrows a small monster token "whose color differs from any other monsters", but a haunt revealed later may bring monsters of that colour.
rulings.resolution: in this digital version the Dog has a marker of its own, not a monster token, so it can never be mistaken for a monster or counted among a haunt's tokens. The colour rule exists only to tell pieces apart on a physical table.

rulings.note: The card does not list which rooms count as one-way passages or rooms that require a roll.
rulings.resolution: the Dog can't go through the Collapsed Room, Coal Chute, Gallery or Mystic Slide (one-way), the Revolving Wall (needs a roll), or the Mystic Elevator. Monsters don't slow it, and it can't carry a haunt item that makes its carrier spend two moves to enter a room. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the official list names the one-way rooms and the Revolving Wall, but not the rooms that take a roll to leave (Junk Room, Attic, Graveyard, Pentagram Chamber), the barrier rooms (Tower, Chasm, Catacombs), or the Secret Passage and Secret Stairs.
rulings.resolution: the Dog doesn't go into a room that takes a roll to leave, or set out from one, since it couldn't get back to its holder without the roll; it may go into a barrier room by the side it comes in on, but never crosses it, as crossing takes a roll. It moves only by doors and stairs, as the card says, so it doesn't use the Secret Passage or the Secret Stairs, whose cards let explorers use them. This reads "rooms that require a roll" by what the Dog would need to do, and keeps its trip a simple out-and-back. Research: only the official FAQ list above.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say where an item ends up after the Dog's trip, or what becomes of an item it carries when it is lost or its holder dies.
rulings.resolution: the Dog's trip is one action that ends back with its holder, so it never holds an item between turns. An item it picks up (from an item pile, in a room it reaches) goes straight into its holder's possession when it returns; an item its holder gives it can be dropped in a room it reaches, onto that room's item pile. It doesn't trade with other explorers, since the card names only picking up, carrying and dropping. With nothing ever left on the Dog, losing it or its holder's death moves no item except as the usual rules say for the holder's own items. The one BGG answer on how the Dog works reads it the same way, as a six-room "boomerang" fetch. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/610370, https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the card says the Dog may pick up, carry or drop "1 item", and doesn't say whether an omen counts.
rulings.resolution: items only, never an omen. The rulebook names omens beside items wherever a rule covers both ("a tradable item or omen", p. 13), so "1 item" on its own means an item card, and most omens only "work like items" (p. 20) without being them. Research: no ruling found.

rulings.note: the official list says the Dog can't go "through" the Collapsed Room or the Gallery, which both have ordinary doors as well as a one-way fall.
rulings.resolution: the Dog may go into either room, and on through it, by its doors, but never takes the fall. What makes them one-way is the fall, as with the Mystic Slide, whose room the Dog is never kept out of; the Coal Chute differs because entering it is the slide. The card already limits the Dog to doors and stairs, so this keeps the official list's sense without closing off rooms an explorer walks through freely. Research: only the official FAQ list above.

drip-drip-drip.title: Drip . . . Drip . . . Drip . . .
lines: Put the Drip token in this room.
While an explorer is in this room, that explorer rolls 1 fewer die on every trait roll, to a "minimum of 1".

rulings.note: the title is printed in three lines as "DRIP . . . / DRIP . . . / DRIP . . ."; the spacing of the ellipses is as printed.
rulings.resolution: no outside ruling is needed; this is a note on the printed title, not a rules question.

rulings.note: the card says "trait rolls" without saying whether an attack, which is rolled on a trait, counts as one.
rulings.resolution: attacks are not trait rolls, so the Drip never removes a die from combat. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

dynamite.title: Dynamite
lines: Instead of attacking, you may throw the Dynamite through a connecting door into an adjacent room.
Every explorer and monster in that room that has both Might and Speed traits must attempt a Speed roll (results below).
Discard this item after you use it.
Roll: Result
5+: Take no damage from Dynamite.
0–4: Take 4 points of physical damage.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say what physical damage does to a monster, which normally isn't damaged but stunned or killed when defeated.
rulings.resolution: A monster that fails the roll is treated as if it had been defeated in physical combat, so it is stunned or killed as its haunt says. A monster that can't be attacked physically, such as a ghost, or that starts the haunt without a Might or a Speed, is unaffected. The traitor can't ignore the Dynamite, since it is an item, not an event. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the card says you throw it "instead of attacking", and no one may attack before the haunt (rules p. 13). It doesn't say whether it can be thrown before the haunt.
rulings.resolution: it can't. Throwing it takes the place of your one attack of the turn, so it can be thrown only when you could attack instead, and it uses up that attack. Research: no ruling found.

effigy.title: Effigy
lines: While you have the Effigy, add 1 die to all trait rolls, except when you attack or defend.
If you ever lose or drop the Effigy, reduce each of your traits by 1 die.

rulings.note: "Reduce each of your traits by 1 die" is printed as-is and is unclear. It may mean 1 step on each trait track.
rulings.resolution: No official, designer or community ruling found; the BGG Rules forum has no thread on the Effigy, and the Widow's Walk FAQ doesn't mention it.

flytrap.title: Flytrap
lines: Take 1 die of physical damage.
Put a Plant token in your room, and keep this card.
After the haunt has been revealed, whenever any hero, traitor or monster enters that room, you may make a Might 7 attack against that opponent.

rulings.note: "that opponent" is used even for an entering hero or traitor who may be on your side; the card does not say whether you may attack an ally. The card also does not say who rolls for the attack if you have died.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found on either point. The only BGG thread on the card asks something else (whether a figure that stays in the room can be attacked again; the single reply says only on entering). Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1677176

footsteps.title: Footsteps
lines: Roll 1 die. An explorer in the Chapel rolls 1 extra die on this roll.
Roll: Result
4: You and the nearest explorer each gain 1 Might.
3: You gain 1 Might, and the nearest explorer loses 1 Sanity.
2: Lose 1 Sanity.
1: Lose 1 Speed.
0: Every explorer loses 1 point from a trait of their own choice.

rulings.note: results 3 and 4 are only reachable with the Chapel's extra die. The card says "an explorer in the Chapel" rather than "you", so it can be read as some other explorer in the Chapel rolling a die too.
rulings.resolution: the extra die goes only to the explorer who drew the card, and only if that explorer is in the Chapel; another explorer standing in the Chapel rolls nothing. Without it, only results 0–2 are possible. Several independent BGG answers agree. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1237066, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/688194

rulings.note: "Nearest explorer" has no tie-break rule.
rulings.resolution: nearest means the fewest rooms entered along the route (movement penalties don't count), and when explorers tie, you choose among them. Every haunt that breaks a nearest or closest tie gives the choice to the player choosing (10, 29, 66, the star haunt), and haunts 11 and 28 measure closest along a route. No card-specific source exists at any level. Earlier research: no ruling found.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say what happens when no other explorer can be reached by any route (all of them cut off in a part of the house there is no way into from yours).
rulings.resolution: then no explorer is nearest, and the part of the result that names them does nothing; you still gain your 1 Might. Nearness is measured along routes (the ruling above), so an explorer with no route to them is not near at all, and the card's own gain doesn't depend on anyone else's. Research: the case isn't discussed anywhere.

funeral.title: Funeral
lines: You must attempt a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 Sanity.
2–3: Lose 1 Sanity.
0–1: Lose 1 Sanity and 1 Might. Then, if the Graveyard or the Crypt has been discovered, put your explorer in one of those rooms (your choice).

ghost-in-the-machine.title: Ghost in the Machine
lines: You must attempt a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
0–2: Lose 1 Might. Keep this card in front of you. Until the start of your next turn, every explorer can move only 1 space per turn; then discard this card.
3+: Draw a roof tile from the room stack, place it in the house, and put your figure in that room.

rulings.note: the 3+ result does not say what happens if no roof tile is left in the room stack, or if it cannot be placed.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found; the Widow's Walk FAQ does not mention this card.

girl.title: Girl
lines: Gain 1 Sanity and 1 Knowledge now.
If you lose custody of the Girl, lose 1 Sanity and 1 Knowledge.
This omen can't be dropped, traded, or stolen.
Make a haunt roll now.

grave-dirt.title: Grave Dirt
lines: You must attempt a Might roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 Might.

0–3: Keep this card. At the start of each of your turns, take 1 point of physical damage. Discard this card if an item card raises one of your traits, or if you end your turn in the Balcony, Gardens, Graveyard, Gymnasium, Larder, Patio, or Tower.

groundskeeper.title: Groundskeeper
lines: You must attempt a Knowledge roll. An explorer in the Gardens rolls 2 fewer dice on this roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Draw an item card.
0–3: The player on your right makes a Might 4 attack against you on behalf of the Groundskeeper. You defend normally, rolling dice equal to your Might.

hanged-men.title: Hanged Men
lines: You must attempt a separate roll for each of your four traits (Speed, Might, Sanity, Knowledge).
If all 4 rolls come up 2+, gain 1 extra point in a trait of your choice.
Roll: Result
2+: That trait is not affected.
0–1: Lose 1 from that trait.

healing-salve.title: Healing Salve
lines: You may apply the Healing Salve to yourself or to another living explorer in the same room.
If that explorer's Might or Speed is below its starting value, raise one or both of those traits to its starting value.
Discard this item after you use it.

hideous-shriek.title: Hideous Shriek
lines: Every explorer must attempt a Sanity roll.
Each result applies only to the explorer who rolled it.
Roll: Result
4+: Nothing happens.
1–3: Take 1 die of mental damage.
0: Take 2 dice of mental damage.

holy-symbol.title: Holy Symbol
lines: Gain 2 Sanity now.
If you lose the Holy Symbol, lose 2 Sanity.
Make a haunt roll now.

idol.title: Idol
lines: Once per turn, before you make any trait, combat or event roll, you may rub the Idol to add 2 dice to that roll (maximum of 8 dice).
Each time you do, lose 1 Sanity.

rulings.note: The card says "once per turn", not "once during your turn", and doesn't say whether a combat roll includes a defense roll on another player's turn.
rulings.resolution: It can be used when you defend, since it isn't a weapon, and "once per turn" allows one use in each player's turn. Two independent answers agree, with no official ruling. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1909175

rulings.note: The card doesn't define an "event roll".
rulings.resolution: an event roll is any roll an event card has you make, its damage dice included; the haunt roll and an item's own dice are not, because the card names the source of the roll, not its kind.

image-in-the-mirror-give.title: Image in the Mirror
lines: If you have no item cards, this event instead affects the next explorer to your left who has an item card. If no explorer has an item card, discard this card.
Choose one of your item cards (an item, "not an omen card") and put it into the item stack, then shuffle that stack.
Gain 1 Knowledge.

rulings.note: there are two different cards named Image in the Mirror (this one and 22). This one gives an item away; the other draws one.
rulings.resolution: no outside ruling is needed; both cards are in the deck as printed. The 1st-edition FAQ's correction to this pair (ignore the "If you don't have any item cards" text on the card that draws an item) is already printed on the 2nd-edition cards: only this card carries that text. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

image-in-the-mirror-take.title: Image in the Mirror
lines: Draw an item card.

rulings.note: this card has no bold story line; its whole flavour paragraph (the mirror and "THIS WILL HELP") is story, and its only rule is drawing an item card.
rulings.resolution: the card has no condition on who is affected; whoever draws it draws an item card. The 1st-edition printing carried the "If you don't have any item cards…" condition on this card too, and the 1st-edition FAQ said to ignore it; the 2nd-edition card drops it. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

it-is-meant-to-be.title: It Is Meant to Be
lines: Choose one of 2 options:
Option 1: look at the top 3 tiles or cards of any one stack. If you do, put those 3 back on top of that stack in any order you like. Don't tell anyone what they were.

Option 2: roll 4 dice and record the total. For one later die roll of your choice that you attempt, you may use that recorded number instead of rolling. If the number is higher than the highest result that roll could produce, use that maximum instead.

rulings.note: Option 2 says "one future die roll of your choice that you attempt", which leaves open whether a roll someone else makes against you (for example, an attack's opposing roll) can be replaced.
rulings.resolution: only a roll you make yourself can be replaced. The 1st-edition FAQ ruled this, and the 2nd-edition card's "that you attempt" wording carries it. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the card doesn't say whether the recorded number can replace a roll you make on another player's turn, such as a defence roll.
rulings.resolution: it can't. The Angel Feather, the Lucky Stone and the Skull omen are the only cards a player may use outside their own turn (the 1st-edition FAQ, quoted under the Angel Feather). Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

jonahs-turn.title: Jonah's Turn
lines: If any explorer has the Puzzle Box, that explorer discards it and draws a replacement item card.
If that happened, you gain 1 Sanity. Otherwise, you take 1 die of mental damage.

key.title: Key
lines: Add 4 dice to trait rolls made to open, or take something from, a card or room tile (for example the Locked Room, Safe, or Vault).
You may pass through the Locked Room without removing a Lock.
At the start of each turn, if you are next to an unlocked door in the Locked Room, you may put a Lock token on that door.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: No 8-dice maximum is printed on the Key (unlike Bloodstone and Spear). The card says "at the start of each turn", not "each of your turns", so it is unclear whether you may lock a door at the start of other players' turns.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found on either point. Players disagree on whether rolls may exceed 8 dice when a card gives no cap. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2501599, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1807098

letter.title: Letter
lines: When you draw this card, you may immediately give one of your explorer tokens to another explorer.
On any of your turns, including the one you drew it on, you may move to that explorer's room; then you discard this omen and that explorer discards your explorer token.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: The printed card does not say when the token is handed over, or whether you may move to that explorer on the turn you draw the Letter. The text above includes the official correction.
rulings.resolution: the Widow's Walk FAQ (updated 12/6/16) corrects the card: you hand over the token immediately on drawing the Letter, and you may move to that explorer on any of your turns, including that one. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1700604/widows-walk-faq (the FAQ PDF, "Widow's Walk FAQ KB 12.6.16", linked from that thread; it is a longer version of https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf)

lightning-strikes.title: Lightning Strikes
lines: Every explorer who is on the roof or in an outside room must attempt a Might roll.
Roll: Result
0: Take 2 points of physical damage.
1–3: Take 1 point of physical damage.
4+: Nothing happens.

rulings.note: this card affects explorers by location, so it may not affect the explorer who drew it. The card does not define "outside room" (presumably rooms marked as outdoor, plus the Widow's Walk roof).
rulings.resolution: no ruling found, and neither the Widow's Walk FAQ nor the base rulebook lists the "outside" rooms; the rulebook only gives the Patio as an example of an outside area. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

lights-out.title: Lights Out
lines: Keep this card. While you hold it, you can move only 1 space per turn.
When you end your turn in the same room as another explorer, discard this card at the end of that turn; from then on you move normally.
Also discard this card if you have the Candle or you end your turn in the Furnace Room.

locked-safe.title: Locked Safe
lines: Put the Safe token in this room.
Once during each explorer's turn, that explorer may attempt a Knowledge roll to open the Safe.
Roll: Result
5+: Draw 2 item cards and remove the Safe token.
2–4: Take 1 die of physical damage. The Safe stays closed.
0–1: Take 2 dice of physical damage. The Safe stays closed.

rulings.note: as with Closet Door, the card does not say the explorer must be in the Safe's room to roll.
rulings.resolution: you must be in the Safe's room to roll, as with the Closet. Research: no ruling found. The 1st-edition FAQ only confirms that the Safe and a room's own roll (such as the Vault's) can both be tried on the same turn. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

locket.title: Locket
lines: Gain 1 Sanity.
Every time you take mental damage ("not just once per turn"), reduce that damage by 1 point.
If you lose this card, lose 1 Sanity.

lucky-stone.title: Lucky Stone
lines: After you attempt a roll of any kind, you may rub the stone once to reroll any number of the dice from that roll.
Discard this item after you use it.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether it can be used outside your own turn, such as on a defense roll.
rulings.resolution: It can. The Angel Feather, the Lucky Stone and the Skull omen are the only cards a player may use outside their own turn. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

madman.title: Madman
lines: Gain 2 Might and lose 1 Sanity now.
If you lose custody of the Madman, lose 2 Might and gain 1 Sanity.
This omen can't be dropped, traded, or stolen.
Make a haunt roll now.

mask.title: Mask
lines: Once during your turn, you may attempt a Sanity roll to use the Mask, with the results below.
Make a haunt roll now.
Roll: Result
4+: You may put on or take off the Mask. Putting it on: gain 2 Knowledge and lose 2 Sanity. Taking it off: gain 2 Sanity and lose 2 Knowledge.
0–3: You can't use the Mask this turn.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say what happens to the traits it changed when you lose the Mask while wearing it.
rulings.resolution: losing the Mask while wearing it takes it off, reversing the change, because the trait change belongs to wearing the card and a card you no longer hold can't be worn.

medallion.title: Medallion
lines: You are immune to the effects of the Pentagram Chamber, Crypt, and Graveyard.
Make a haunt roll now.

medical-kit.title: Medical Kit
lines: Once during your turn, you may attempt a Knowledge roll to heal yourself or another explorer in the same room (results below).
The Medical Kit can't raise a trait above its starting value.
Roll: Result
8+: Gain up to 3 points of physical traits.
6–7: Gain up to 2 points of physical traits.
4–5: Gain 1 point in a physical trait.
0–3: Nothing happens.

mists-from-the-walls.title: Mists from the Walls
lines: Every explorer in the basement must make a Sanity roll.
Each explorer's result applies only to that explorer.
Roll: Result
4+: Nothing happens.
1–3: Take 1 die of mental damage, plus 1 more die of damage if that explorer is in a room with an event symbol.
0: Take 1 die of mental damage, plus 2 more dice of damage if that explorer is in a room with an event symbol.

rulings.note: the extra dice are printed only as "additional dice of damage" without saying mental; read in context they are most likely mental damage too.
rulings.resolution: the additional dice are mental damage. The whole card is a Sanity roll dealing mental damage, and "additional" adds to that damage. Research: no ruling found. Searched the 1st-edition FAQ, the Widow's Walk FAQ and the BGG Betrayal rules forum (no thread discusses this card); tkindy/betrayal's card data has the same wording. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

misty-arch.title: Misty Arch
lines: Walking through the arch is optional.
If you do, take your figure out of the house and roll 3 dice; where you end up depends on the result.
Roll: Result
0: Put your figure in the Entrance Hall and discard one item card.
1–2: Put your figure in the Entrance Hall and flip your character card over, resetting every trait to its starting value.
3–4: Put your figure in any room that has an open doorway.
5–6: Put your figure in any room that has an open doorway, then draw an item card.

rulings.note: the printed card offers the choice to walk through, then says "Remove your figure" with no condition, which can read as if the roll happens either way. The text above follows the official correction.
rulings.resolution: errata. Walking through is not required, and the roll happens only if you do: the card's "Remove your figure" should read "If you do, remove your figure". Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

music-box.title: Music Box
lines: Once per turn, you may open or close the Music Box.

While the Music Box is open, any explorer or monster with a Sanity trait that enters the Music Box's room, or starts its turn there, must make a Sanity roll of 4+. If it fails, that explorer or monster is mesmerized by the music and its turn ends.
If an explorer or monster carrying the Music Box is mesmerized, it drops the Music Box. If the Music Box was open when dropped, it stays open.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether the explorer carrying an open Music Box is affected by it.
rulings.resolution: they are affected like anyone else, including in each room they enter with it, because the music fills the room the box is in and the carrier is in that room.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say what happens to an explorer mesmerized when it isn't their turn.
rulings.resolution: they only drop the Music Box if they carry it; there is no turn of theirs to end, because the card's "its turn ends" can only cut short a turn being played.

rulings.note: The card says only that an open box dropped by a mesmerized carrier stays open.
rulings.resolution: the Music Box stays open through every drop and trade until someone closes it, because open is the box's own state and the card gives no other way to close it.

mutant-housepet.title: Mutant Housepet
lines: You must make a Speed roll of 4+.
On a failure, take 1 point of physical damage.
On a success, gain 1 Sanity and 1 Speed.

mystic-slide.title: Mystic Slide
lines: Redirect (printed above the story text): if you are in the basement, this event instead affects the next explorer to your left who is not in the basement. If every explorer is in the basement, discard this card.
Place the Slide token in this room, then make a Might roll to use the Slide.
On later turns, any explorer may make this same roll to use the Slide.
Roll: Result
5+: You control the Slide: put yourself in any explored room on any floor below the Slide.

0–4: Draw room tiles from the stack until you draw a basement room, and place that tile (if the stack has no basement rooms, choose a basement room already in play). You fall to that room and take 1 die of physical damage. If it is not your turn, don't draw a card for that room.

rulings.note: on the 0–4 result the card does not say what happens to the non-basement tiles drawn before the basement room is found.
rulings.resolution: Draw from the top of the room stack, as when exploring: a tile that can't go on the floor goes face down on the room discard pile. If the stack runs out, shuffle the discard pile into a new stack (rules.md, p. 9) and keep drawing; only when no basement tile is left anywhere do you choose a basement room in play, as the card says. This is the same rule as every "draw until a room fits" effect (see Collapsed Room in rules.md). Research: no ruling found. The 1st-edition FAQ rules only that "a floor below the Slide" means any lower floor (which the 2nd-edition wording already says), and the one BGG answer on placement says the sliding explorer chooses where the new basement room goes; neither covers the skipped tiles. Searched both FAQs and the BGG rules forum's Mystic Slide threads. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3084734

rulings.note: when the event passes to another explorer, the card doesn't say whose room "this room" is.
rulings.resolution: the Slide goes in the room of the explorer the event affects, who makes the roll there. The redirect exists so that the Slide never starts in the basement, which only works if it goes where the affected explorer stands.

night-view.title: Night View
lines: You must make a Knowledge roll.
Roll: Result
5+: Gain 1 Knowledge.
0–4: Nothing happens.

phone-call.title: Phone Call
lines: Roll 2 dice (not a trait roll). Each result also has a quoted line spoken by a granny voice, which is flavour only.
Roll: Result
4: Gain 1 Sanity.
3: Gain 1 Knowledge.
1–2: Take 1 die of mental damage.
0: Take 2 dice of physical damage.

photograph.title: Photograph
lines: When you discover a room, you may discard the first room tile drawn and instead discover the next eligible room in the room stack.
Make a haunt roll now.

pickpokets-gloves.title: Pickpoket's Gloves
lines: When you are in the same room as another explorer, you may discard this item to take any item that explorer is carrying.

rulings.note: The title is printed "PICKPOKET'S GLOVES", a misprint of "Pickpocket's". It's kept as printed here. Haunt 100 (Let's Play a Game) names the card "Pickpocket Gloves".
rulings.resolution: The name is a misprint: Haunt 100 spells it with "Pickpocket", and the open-source card data (tkindy/betrayal) uses "Pickpocket's Gloves". Search for the card under either spelling. Source: https://github.com/tkindy/betrayal

rulings.note: the card says "take", not "steal", so it is unclear whether items and omens that can't be stolen (the Armor, the Box, the companions) are protected from it, and whether the Blood Dagger's "if it is stolen" damage applies.
rulings.resolution: taking with the gloves is stealing, without the attack. The gloves can take any item or omen the other explorer could lose to a steal: not the Armor, not an omen marked "can't be stolen", but the Blood Dagger (its holder takes the 2 dice of physical damage) and any tradable omen or haunt item token, unless a haunt forbids stealing. The take counts as the steal action for that item this turn. Otherwise a single discarded card would undo every "can't be stolen" line in the game, which those lines exist to prevent; the one BGG answer on omens (thread 610370) also lets the gloves take whatever the stealing rules allow, and thread 1414426 treats the take as a steal for the one-action limit. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/610370, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1414426

possession.title: Possession
lines: Choose any one trait and make a roll for it.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 in a trait of your choice.
0–3: The chosen trait drops to its lowest value (not to the skull). If that trait is already at its lowest value, lower a different trait to its lowest value instead.

rulings.note: on 4+ the card says "a trait of your choice", so the gained trait need not be the one you rolled. On 0–3 the card doesn't say who picks the "different trait"; presumably you do.
rulings.resolution: you choose the different trait, as you choose every other trait on this card. Research: no ruling found. Searched the 1st-edition FAQ, the Widow's Walk FAQ and the BGG rules forum; no thread discusses this card. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

puzzle-box.title: Puzzle Box
lines: Once during your turn, you may attempt a Knowledge roll to open the box (results below).
Roll: Result
6+: You open the box. Draw 2 item cards and discard the Puzzle Box.
0–5: You just can't get it open.

rabbits-foot.title: Rabbit's Foot
lines: Once during your turn, you may reroll 1 die. You must keep the second roll.

revolver.title: Revolver
lines: You may use the Revolver to attack with Speed instead of Might. Your opponent then defends with Speed and takes physical damage.
Roll 1 extra die on your Speed attack roll (maximum of 8 dice).
With the Revolver, you may attack anyone in the same room or within line of sight ("through an uninterrupted straight line of doors").
If you attack someone in another room and lose, you take no damage.
You can't use another weapon while using this one.

revolving-wall.title: Revolving Wall
lines: Place the Wall Switch token on a wall of this room that has no exit, or on "a corner of this room".
If there is no room on the other side of the Wall Switch, draw room tiles until you find one for this floor and put it in the house there. If this floor has no rooms left, discard this card.
Then put your explorer in that room (the one on the other side).
Once during an explorer's turn, if that explorer is in either room, they may make a Knowledge roll to use the Wall Switch.
Roll: Result
3+: That explorer finds the switch and goes through to the other room. This doesn't count as moving a space.
0–2: That explorer can't find the switch and can't go through.

rulings.note: the card does not say what happens to room tiles drawn that are not for this floor. It also doesn't say whether the move into the other room happens if the card was discarded for lack of rooms (presumably not, since the card is gone).
rulings.resolution: Draw from the top of the room stack, as when exploring: a tile that can't go on the floor goes face down on the room discard pile. If the stack runs out, shuffle the discard pile into a new stack (rules.md, p. 9) and keep drawing. "This floor has no rooms left" means no tile for this floor is left in the stack or the discard pile; then the card is discarded, you don't move, and the Wall Switch token goes with the card. This is the same rule as every "draw until a room fits" effect (see Collapsed Room in rules.md). Research: no ruling found on either question. The 1st-edition FAQ's Revolving Wall errata (icons in the new room do affect you) corrects a sentence the 2nd-edition card no longer prints; BGG threads cover corner placement and how the new room must be oriented, not these points. Searched both FAQs and the BGG rules forum's Revolving Wall threads. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1696618, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1699848

rulings.note: the card doesn't say which room lies beyond "a corner of this room", which spots may be chosen, how a new room beyond the switch is turned, or what happens to the switch when either room later moves (What The...?, the Mystic Elevator).
rulings.resolution: a corner leads to the room diagonally beyond it, the only room a corner touches that a wall doesn't; it is how a room with an exit on every wall (the Ballroom) can have a switch at all. You choose any wall without an exit or any corner, but only one with a room beyond it or a room left that can go there, so the choice never strands the card. A new room beyond the switch goes any way round, lining up as many doors as it can without sealing a floor, as exploration places it, and you draw its card (the 1st-edition FAQ errata). The switch belongs to the wall of the room it was put on: it moves and turns with that room, and leads to whatever room lies beyond that wall, if any. A token on the room it marks is what moves with a tile everywhere else (rules.md, Mystic Elevator), so the switch does the same.

ring.title: Ring
lines: When you attack an opponent that has a Sanity trait, you may attack with Sanity instead of Might. The opponent then defends with Sanity, and the damage is mental instead of physical.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: the card speaks of attacking "an opponent", and before the haunt no one is anyone's opponent; yet a card can make you attack before the haunt (the Bloody Vision).
rulings.resolution: the explorer you attack is your opponent for that attack, so the Ring can be used in any attack you make, before the haunt too. The card's limit is the opponent's Sanity trait, not their side. Research: no ruling found.

rope.title: Rope
lines: You may move up the Coal Chute, and from the Ballroom to the Gallery.
You don't need to roll to cross the Chasm.
You take no damage from the Collapsed Room.
You may move from the room with the Below Collapsed Room token into the Collapsed Room.
When moving by a dumbwaiter (dumbwaiter icon printed), you may move to any landing.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: The dumbwaiter is shown as a small icon inline in the text, not a word; it refers to rooms bearing that symbol (Widow's Walk).
rulings.resolution: the Widow's Walk rule sheet defines dumbwaiter rooms as the tiles with that symbol and lists the landings as the Basement Landing, any room of the Grand Staircase/Foyer/Entrance Hall, the Upper Landing and the Roof Landing. Source: Widow's Walk rule sheet, p. 2 (widows-walk-rules.md); https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2369803

rotten.title: Rotten
lines: You must make a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
5+: Gain 1 Sanity.
2–4: Lose 1 Might.
1: Lose 1 Might and 1 Speed.
0: Lose 1 Might, 1 Speed, 1 Knowledge, and 1 Sanity.

sacrificial-dagger.title: Sacrificial Dagger
lines: When you make a Might attack with this weapon, roll 3 extra dice (maximum of 8 dice). You must first make a Knowledge roll (results below).
You can't use another weapon while using this one.
Roll: Result
6+: No effect.
3–5: Lose 1 from a mental trait.
0–2: The dagger twists in your hand! Take 2 dice of physical damage. You can't attack this turn.

secret-passage.title: Secret Passage
lines: Put one Secret Passage token in this room. Roll 3 dice and put the second Secret Passage token in a room chosen by the result (see table).
You may then use the Secret Passage, even if you have no movement left.
Moving from one Secret Passage token to the other counts as moving one space; the passage itself is not a space.
On later turns, any explorer may use the Secret Passage. An explorer can't end their turn in the passage.
Roll: Result
6: Any existing room.
4–5: Any existing upper floor room.
2–3: Any existing ground floor room.
0–1: Any existing basement room.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say who chooses the room within the rolled floor (presumably you).
rulings.resolution: you choose the room on the rolled floor; you are the card's "you". Research: no ruling found. The 1st-edition FAQ settles only that the second token goes in an already-discovered room, uses no door, and costs one space to cross. Searched both FAQs and the BGG rules forum's Secret Passage threads. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

secret-stairs.title: Secret Stairs
lines: Put one Secret Stairs token in this room and a second Secret Stairs token in an existing room on a different floor.
Moving from one Secret Stairs token to the other counts as moving one space; the stairs themselves are not a space.
You may follow the stairs immediately, even if you have no movement left. If you follow them this turn, draw an event card in the room you arrive in.

rulings.note: unlike Secret Passage, the card does not say that other explorers may use the stairs on later turns, though the tokens stay in place.
rulings.resolution: the stairs stay usable. The 1st-edition FAQ, answering whether an event is drawn each time the Secret Stairs are used, says only the explorer who drew the card draws one, and only on using them right away; it also lets monsters use the Secret Stairs. Both answers treat the stairs as a lasting route for later users, and the one BGG answer on the question agrees. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1309984

shrieking-wind.title: Shrieking Wind
lines: Every explorer in the Gardens, Graveyard, Patio, Tower, on the Balcony, or in a room with an outside-facing window must make a Might roll.
Each explorer's result applies only to that explorer.
Roll: Result
5+: Nothing happens.
3–4: Take 1 die of physical damage.
1–2: Take 1 die of mental damage.
0: Take 1 die of physical damage, and put one of your items (if you have any) in the Entrance Hall.

silence.title: Silence
lines: Every explorer in the basement must make a Sanity roll.
Each explorer's result applies only to that explorer.
Roll: Result
4+: Nothing happens.
1–3: Take 1 die of mental damage.
0: Take 2 dice of mental damage.

skeletons.title: Skeletons
lines: Put the Skeletons token in this room. Take 1 die of mental damage.
Once during an explorer's turn, that explorer may make a Sanity roll to search the Skeletons.
Each result applies only to the explorer who rolled.
Roll: Result
5+: Draw an item card and remove the Skeletons token.
0–4: Nothing found; take 1 die of mental damage.

rulings.note: the card doesn't explicitly require the searching explorer to be in the Skeletons' room, though that is the evident intent.
rulings.resolution: you must be in the room with the Skeletons token to search, as with the Closet. Research: no ruling found. Searched both FAQs and the BGG rules forum; the Skeletons threads cover traitors and whether drawing an item ends movement, not where the searcher must stand. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2353297, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/930903

skull.title: Skull
lines: Whenever you take mental damage, you may take all of it as physical damage instead.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether damage taken as physical instead of mental counts as physical damage for other cards, such as the Armor.
rulings.resolution: it does: the damage is physical from then on, so the Armor takes 1 off it, because "take it as physical damage" makes it physical damage in every respect.

smelling-salts.title: Smelling Salts
lines: If your Knowledge, or the Knowledge of another living explorer in the same room, is below its starting value, you may use the Smelling Salts to raise that trait to its starting value.
Discard this item after you use it.

rulings.note: The card is printed "If your or another living explorer's Knowledge ... and you're in the same room", which reads awkwardly when you use it on yourself. The "same room" condition applies to the other explorer.
rulings.resolution: You can use the Smelling Salts on yourself. Neither they nor the Healing Salve can revive a dead explorer. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

smoke.title: Smoke
lines: Put the Smoke token in this room.
The Smoke blocks line of sight from adjacent rooms.
While in this room, an explorer rolls 2 fewer dice on all trait rolls (minimum of 1 die).

rulings.note: "blocks line of sight from adjacent rooms" doesn't say whether someone in the Smoke can see out, or whether the Smoke blocks a line that runs through its room.
rulings.resolution: line of sight is mutual, so the Smoke blocks it into, out of and through its room. A distance attack needs line of sight between attacker and target whichever of them is in the Smoke, and smoke that hid a room but let sight pass through it would make no sense at the table. Research: no ruling found in the 1st-edition FAQ.

snake-oil.title: Snake Oil
lines: Discard this item to choose an explorer in your room (you may choose yourself). Raise one of that explorer's physical traits and/or one of their mental traits to its starting value.

rulings.note: The card doesn't say whether this works only on a trait that is below its starting value. It also doesn't say whether a trait above its starting value would be lowered.
rulings.resolution: No official, designer or community ruling found. The only BGG post naming the Snake Oil describes a player using it to raise traits that were below their starting values, which doesn't settle either question. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1731166

something-hidden.title: Something Hidden
lines: You may choose to make a Knowledge roll to work out what's odd; if you don't, nothing happens.
Roll: Result
4+: Draw an item card.
0–3: Lose 1 Sanity.

something-slimy.title: Something Slimy
lines: You must make a Speed roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 Speed.
1–3: Lose 1 Might.
0: Lose 1 Might and 1 Speed.

spear.title: Spear
lines: When making a Might attack with the Spear, roll 2 additional dice (maximum of 8 dice).
You can't use another weapon while using this one.
Make a haunt roll now.

spider.title: Spider
lines: You must make either a Speed roll or a Sanity roll (your choice).
Roll: Result
4+: Gain 1 in the trait you rolled.
1–3: Take 1 die of physical damage.
0: Take 2 dice of physical damage.

spirit-board.title: Spirit Board
lines: Before you move during your turn, you may look at the top tile of the room stack.
If you use the Spirit Board after the haunt is revealed, the traitor may move any number of monsters 1 space closer to you. (If you are the traitor, you don't have to move those monsters.)
If there is no traitor, all monsters move 1 space closer to you.
Make a haunt roll now.

rulings.note: "you don't have to move those monsters" when you are the traitor reads as the traitor's movement being optional; the card gives no further detail.
rulings.resolution: moving the monsters is optional for the traitor: any number of them, zero included, 1 space closer, as the card says ("you don't have to move those monsters"). Stunned monsters can be moved this way (https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/994104). Research: no ruling found. Forum threads on the Spirit Board settle only that the looked-at tile stays on top of the stack. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1872346, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/854312

rulings.note: the card doesn't say what moving a monster "1 space closer" involves.
rulings.resolution: the same as the Bell's pull (cards/items.md): one room nearer along a route, through a connecting door. It spends no movement, ignores the slowing from opponents, and gives the monster no attack or other action.

rulings.note: "before you move" doesn't say whether being put in another room without spending movement (a fall, a card, crossing a barrier) counts as moving.
rulings.resolution: you have moved once you have spent movement this turn; being put somewhere without spending any doesn't count, so the board can still be used after it. The board is for planning where you will explore, which spending movement is, and a fall or a card's move doesn't use up any of that. Research: no ruling found.

teapot.title: Teapot
lines: Once during your turn, when an explorer in your room (yourself included) takes physical damage, you may draw an item card.
If you are, or become, the traitor, shuffle this item card into the item stack.

the-beckoning.title: The Beckoning
lines: Every explorer in the Gardens, Graveyard, Tower, on the Balcony, or in a room with an outside-facing window must make a Sanity roll.
Each explorer's result applies only to that explorer.
Roll: Result
3+: Nothing happens.

0–2: You jump to the Patio. If the Patio isn't in the house, search the room stack for it, put it in the house, and shuffle the stack. Put your explorer in the Patio and take 1 die of physical damage.

rulings.note: unlike Shrieking Wind, the Patio is not in this card's list of affected rooms.
rulings.resolution: an explorer on the Patio is not affected, as printed. The result is a jump to the Patio, which means nothing to someone already there. Research: no ruling found on whether the omission is deliberate; no source treats it as an error. The one BGG thread on the card says the Patio, if not yet in play, is placed legally on the ground floor rather than against the window jumped from. The 1st-edition FAQ adds that you go to the Patio even with no clear path. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2311916, https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: the card says to search the room stack for the Patio, not the room discard pile, and doesn't say what happens if the Patio can't be placed anywhere.
rulings.resolution: search the discard pile too: tiles set aside while exploring are still waiting to enter the house, and a Patio skipped earlier is no less "not in the house". The Patio goes at a legal spot on the ground floor that the jumping explorer chooses, as exploration places it, and they draw its event, as for any room discovered through a card. If it has no legal spot, there is nowhere to jump: nothing happens to that explorer, and the damage, which comes from the jump, isn't taken.

the-left-hand.title: The Left Hand
lines: Choose one of three options:
Cut off your hand: lose 1 Might and gain 1 Sanity.
Replace your hand: lose 1 Might and draw an item card.
Keep your hand: lose 2 Sanity, gain 1 Might, then move to the nearest room with an omen symbol and draw an omen card.

rulings.note: the card doesn't define "nearest" (fewest spaces, presumably) or how to break ties.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found. The Widow's Walk FAQ doesn't mention this card, and no BGG rules-forum thread discusses it. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

the-lost-one.title: The Lost One
lines: You must make a Knowledge roll. On 5 or more, gain 1 Knowledge and nothing else happens.
Otherwise, roll 3 dice to see where you are led (see table).

When a result has you draw a room tile for a specific floor, put that tile in the house and put your explorer there. If you reach the end of the stack without drawing a room for the rolled floor, put your explorer in the Entrance Hall instead.
Roll: Result
6: Put your explorer in the Entrance Hall.
4–5: Put your explorer in the Upper Landing.
2–3: Draw room tiles until you find an upper floor room.
0–1: Draw room tiles until you find a basement room.

rulings.note: the table is for the 3-dice roll, not the Knowledge roll. The card doesn't say what happens to drawn tiles that are not for the target floor.
rulings.resolution: draw from the top of the room stack, putting tiles that aren't for the rolled floor face down on the room discard pile, as when exploring. This card prints its own end ("if you reach the end of the stack"), and a card's rule beats the rulebook (p. 12), so this is one pass through the stack with no reshuffle; then you go to the Entrance Hall. Research: no ruling found on the skipped tiles. The 1st-edition FAQ rules on neighbouring points only: you go to the destination even with no clear path, and if the room you are sent into is newly discovered and has a symbol, you draw that card too. A BGG answer adds that the card's effect lasts only the turn it is drawn. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1782077

rulings.note: the card doesn't say what happens to a tile for the rolled floor that has no legal spot on it (every doorway it could face closed, or it would seal the floor).
rulings.resolution: it is skipped like a tile for another floor, onto the discard pile, and the search goes on. The card has you "put that tile in the house", which a tile with no legal spot can't be, and every "draw until a room fits" effect treats a tile that can't go on the floor the same way (see Mystic Slide). Research: no ruling found.

the-voice.title: The Voice
lines: You must make a Knowledge roll.
Roll: Result
4+: Draw an item card.
0–3: Nothing happens.

the-walls.title: The Walls
lines: Draw the next room tile and put it in the house, then put your explorer in that room.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say whether you draw a card for the new room, or what happens if the drawn tile can't legally be placed.
rulings.resolution: you do draw for the new room. The 1st-edition FAQ names The Walls and rules that a room discovered through an event card's effect makes you draw the card for its symbol. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2015/downloads/ah/FAQ_BHotH_102605-2.pdf

rulings.note: no source covers a drawn tile that has no legal spot anywhere in the house.
rulings.resolution: the card draws as every "draw until a room fits" effect does: a tile with no legal spot goes face down on the room discard pile and you draw again, reshuffling the discards when the stack runs out (rules.md, p. 9). If no tile left can go anywhere, nothing happens and you stay where you are. One draw rule for every card keeps the house legal and is the one players already know from exploring; the card's point is a new room, so a tile that can't be placed is skipped rather than ending it.

the-walls-have-eyes.title: The Walls Have Eyes
lines: You must make a Sanity roll.
Roll: Result
0–2: Lose 1 Sanity.
3: Gain 1 Knowledge.

4+: If the Arsenal is in play, put your figure in the Arsenal and draw an item card. If it isn't in play yet, search the room stack for it, put it in the house, shuffle the stack, and put your figure in the Arsenal "as if you just discovered it".

rulings.note: the table is printed lowest-first, as reproduced. In the not-yet-in-play branch the card doesn't say "draw an item card"; "as if you just discovered it" presumably means you resolve the Arsenal's discovery as normal.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found. The Widow's Walk FAQ doesn't mention this card, and no BGG rules-forum thread discusses it. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

vial.title: Vial
lines: Once on your turn, you may drink from the Vial: roll 2 dice and apply the result below.
Make a haunt roll now.
Roll: Result
0: Take 2 points of physical damage.
1: Take 2 points of mental damage. Draw an item card.
2: No effect.
3: Gain 1 in any physical trait.
4: Gain 1 in each trait except Sanity. Lose 2 Sanity.

rulings.note: The card does not say the Vial is discarded or used up after drinking, so it can apparently be used once every turn.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgameexpansion/198452/betrayal-at-house-on-the-hill-widows-walk/forums/66

webs.title: Webs
lines: You must make a Might roll.
While stuck, you can't do anything until you are freed.

Once during an explorer's turn, any explorer may make a Might roll to free you, and you may also attempt it yourself. A 4+ frees you, but you don't gain the 1 Might. Anyone who fails an attempt can't move for the rest of that turn.
After 3 failed attempts, you break free automatically on your next turn and take that turn normally.
When you are freed, discard this card.
Roll: Result
4+: You break free. Gain 1 Might and discard this card.
0–3: You're stuck. Keep this card.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say whether a rescuer must be in your room, or whether your own initial failed roll counts toward the 3 unsuccessful attempts.
rulings.resolution: a rescuer must be in your room. Two independent BGG answers in separate threads say so and none disagrees, though one later poster asked again without getting an answer, so the support is thin. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/598908, https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/1107717

rulings.note: "Once during an explorer's turn, any explorer may make a Might roll to free you" doesn't say whose turn the attempt is made on.
rulings.resolution: as with the Debris, each explorer may try once during their own turn, and you may try on yours. An explorer acts only on their own turn (rules p. 6), and the Debris, whose mechanism is the same, says so in as many words. Research: no ruling found.

what-the.title: What The . . . ?
lines: Pick up the tile of the room you are in, first setting aside everything on it.
Place it elsewhere on the same floor so that its door connects to a different unexplored doorway, then put back everything you set aside.
If there is no unexplored doorway on this floor, move the room to a different floor.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say whether the starting tiles can be picked up, which way round the moved room goes, or what happens when no floor has an unexplored doorway for it.
rulings.resolution: the starting tiles (the Entrance Hall, Foyer and Grand Staircase tile, and each landing) never move: the first is one tile holding three rooms, and each landing is what its floor is built from, so moving one would pull the house apart. In one of them nothing happens. Otherwise the room goes against a different free doorway on its floor, or, with none, on another floor its back allows, placed as exploration places a tile: a door toward the doorway, as many doors lined up as possible, and no floor sealed, including the one it leaves. With no legal spot anywhere it stays where it is.

what-year-is-it.title: What Year Is It?!
lines: Lose 1 Sanity, and gain 1 Might and 1 Knowledge.
If the haunt has been revealed, the other side must read aloud their italicized opening and closing story text.
If the haunt hasn't been revealed, keep this card in front of you until it is (then the read-aloud above applies).

rulings.note: "the other side" is relative to you once teams exist; the card doesn't say what happens if there is no other side.
rulings.resolution: no ruling found. The Widow's Walk FAQ doesn't mention this card, and no BGG rules-forum thread discusses it. Source: https://media.wizards.com/2016/downloads/widows_walk_faq.pdf

whoops.title: Whoops!
lines: Turn all your item cards face down (omen cards are not included) and shuffle them.
The player to your right discards one of them at random.
Then turn your remaining item cards face up again.

below-collapsed-room.title: Below Collapsed Room
lines: Marks the basement room where the first explorer to fall from the Collapsed Room landed (rules.md, Collapsed Room). The Rope omen lets its holder move from the room with this token up into the Collapsed Room.

blessing.title: Blessing
lines: While a hero is in the Blessing's room, that hero rolls 1 extra die on every trait roll, to a maximum of 8 dice.
Heroes only, not the traitor. Attacks are not trait rolls, so the Blessing never adds a die to an attack (see A Moment of Hope in cards/events.md).

burial-mound.title: Burial Mound
lines: Once the haunt has been revealed, each time an explorer leaves the Burial Mound's room, the corpse attacks that explorer: the player on that explorer's right makes a Might 4 attack against them.
If the explorer wins that fight by 3 or more, discard the Burial Mound token.

closet.title: Closet
lines: Once during each explorer's turn, that explorer may roll 2 dice to open the Closet.
Roll: Result
4: Draw an item card.
2–3: Draw an event card.
0–1: Draw an event card and remove the Closet token.

rulings.note: the card doesn't say the explorer must be in the Closet's room to roll (see Closet Door in cards/events.md).
rulings.resolution: you must be in the Closet's room to roll; see Closet Door in cards/events.md. Research: see the resolution under Closet Door in cards/events.md.

drip.title: Drip
lines: While an explorer is in the Drip's room, that explorer rolls 1 fewer die on every trait roll, to a minimum of 1 die. Attacks are not trait rolls.

fountain.title: Fountain
lines: Placed only by Widow's Walk haunts, never by a card or tile. Each haunt that uses them names what they represent and gives their rules (see the Widow's Walk table above).
The traitor and monsters ignore Obstacle tokens unless a haunt says otherwise (see `widows-walk-rules.md`).
## Pentagonal item tokens
Shape: pentagon. Haunts call them "pentagonal item tokens"; the rulebook glossary says they are numbered.
Base total: 14, made up of:
Token: Count: Numbers: Faces
Item: 10: 1–10: front "ITEM" and a number; back "ITEM" with no number
Item Pile: 4: none: "ITEM PILE" on both sides

Purpose of the numbered Item tokens: haunt-specific objects (the Sarcophagus, Roots, Paint, Parachutes, Keys, the Toy Airplane, and so on). Unless the haunt says otherwise they can be traded, dropped, picked up or stolen like item and omen cards (rules.md, Item Tokens). Haunt 34 hands them out face up by number, 1 up to the number of players.

Purpose of the Item Pile tokens: mark items dropped in a room, including those dropped by a dead explorer or a stunned item-carrying monster. Remove the token when the last item in the pile is picked up (rules.md, Use Item and Omen Cards).
Set: base. Widow's Walk adds none.
## Triangular Trait Roll tokens
Shape: triangle. Haunts call them "triangular <Trait> Roll tokens".
The trait is printed on both sides ("KNOWLEDGE ROLL" and so on). Not numbered.
Purpose: count successful special rolls in a haunt (for example, tokens placed toward a banishing or a rescue, usually up to the number of players).
Token: Set: Count
Knowledge Roll: base: 6
Might Roll: base: 6
Sanity Roll: base: 6
Speed Roll: Widow's Walk replacement sheet (not in the box): 3
Base total 18, matching the rulebook.
## Turn/Damage track
A counter. The base game has one Turn/Damage track (rulebook component list). Haunts use it to count turns or damage: each haunt says what it starts at and when it moves up or down.
Treated as a plain number with no printed range, by the owner's decision. Its physical length matters only if a haunt counts past the end of the track.

rulings.note: the rulebook counts 14 pentagonal tokens without splitting them. 10 are numbered Item tokens, which leaves 4 Item Piles. A player's count of their own box on BoardGameGeek confirms it: "10 numbered items" and "4 item piles" (https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/600958).
rulings.resolution: 10 numbered Item tokens and 4 Item Piles, per one player's count on BoardGameGeek, consistent with the rulebook total. Source: https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/600958

rulings.note: haunts that need more than 10 item tokens at once can run short. The BoardGameGeek thread above was about haunt 34 (Guillotines), where players found more Key locations than numbered tokens.
rulings.resolution: see haunt 34's own notes in haunts/34-guillotines.md (the designer says the collar numbers were meant to be a separate numbered set).

rulings.note: the rulebook counts 18 triangular tokens without splitting them, so the per-trait count of 6 is inferred: 18 split evenly over the three base traits. It fits the haunts, which ask for up to "the number of players" (6) of one trait, and in haunt 49 for 6 Knowledge Roll and 6 Sanity Roll tokens at once. No base haunt uses a Speed Roll token.
rulings.resolution: the split is informational. Supply is unlimited unless a haunt makes running out a rule (see the top of this file). Research: not researched; the inferred split is the only even one.

rulings.note: the Speed Roll tokens were meant for the Widow's Walk sheet but were left off it. The FAQ says to use an item token in their place, or print the replacement sheet.
rulings.resolution: Widow's Walk FAQ. Source: the Widow's Walk FAQ (One of the Master's Affairs; Seasons of the Witch).
